headline: AI WROTE 948
LINUX **EXPLOITS**
cover.image_prompt: Cinematic macro of a massive dark circuit-board vault door, glowing amber traces converging on a heavy closed lock at the center, cold blue light leaking through a thin seam, drifting dust and shallow depth of field. Main subject in the upper half, lower third in deep shadow. No text, no letters, no logos, no people.
cover.hook_pick_reason: The number hook is concrete and fully backed by the lead card (working exploits for 948 of 1,724 reproduced kernel flaws), and it is the story's own card title, so the promise is kept on slide 2. 'Locks up' was dropped because it can read as the model being withheld, while access is only limited to vetted defenders. No reader-impact hook: the lead articles state no effect on ordinary readers, only on security teams and approved customers.

facts.text: OpenAI announced GPT-6 Cyber on Nov 5 (US time); it is built on GPT-6 Astra and specialised in finding vulnerabilities, writing exploit code and penetration testing.
Researchers reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities and wrote working privilege-escalation exploits for 948; GPT-5.6 Sol succeeded on 166 in the same setup.
According to Reuters (as cited by AI타임스), 588 of the 948 were previously unknown flaws.
It found 81 new high-severity vulnerabilities in Mozilla's Firefox; Mozilla fixed many.
On ExploitGym it scored 48.5% vs 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber; it did worse than GPT-6 Astra on FrontierCyber (90 of 288 tasks vs 96).
OpenAI rates its cyber capability 'Critical', the highest level in OpenAI's own safety evaluation, up from 'High' for GPT-5.6 Cyber.

Access is limited to approved customers of Daybreak Red, with identity and permission checks. Per AI타임스, OpenAI plans to widen GPT-6 Cyber to all approved customers over the coming weeks and add a group for critical infrastructure defenders.
Max Justicz, CTO of Charge Robotics, used GPT-5.6 Sol via OpenAI's Daybreak Blue program to find a severe Ubuntu/Debian flaw in two hours; Debian patched it and there is no known exploitation.
OpenAI says it wants to 'dramatically expand Daybreak' to organisations of every size, independent researchers and open-source maintainers (no timeline given in this article).
